title: Course v1
description: A factory course (course factory, F5/CRS1, spec D2): one committed course.yaml plus the Markdown sources it names, both under courses/<id>/ in this repo. The schema defines WHAT a course is -- level, locale, the slide renderer, modules of lessons, the quiz shape, typed variables and licensed asset references -- never the prose itself: every lesson's reading and slides are separate, separately reviewed Markdown files, and no course value is ever free-form HTML or code. 🔴 A SOURCE IS MARKDOWN, NEVER A PROGRAM: the `sources` file names are pinned to `.md`, so a `.py` (or `.html`) source is refused by the contract before any consumer reads it -- the same law F3's template.v1 states for its layout sidecars. Every string a course contributes is one of (a) literal text, (b) a placeholder {{var.<key>}} naming a declared variable, or (c) a token the renderer supplies: {{theme.<token>}}, {{option.<locale|palette>}}, {{kit.<disclaimers|ai_disclosure>}}, {{course.<title|level|locale>}} and {{lesson.<title|module>}}. Fonts are declared under assets.fonts only, images under assets.images, footage under assets.footage, and every asset value is an `asset:<key>` reference resolved by the consumer's asset library -- a raw URL is never a course value, because the licence lives with the asset and never with the document. The human label is `title`, not `name`: `name` is refused by the shared PII property-name denylist (deploys/tests/contracts_lib.py PII_NAMES), which every schema in this repo is checked against. The schema is deliberately SELF-CONTAINED (no $ref, not even to its own branches) so contracts_lib's schema walkers keep working on it.

id.description: Kebab slug; also the directory name under courses/ and the import key.

version.description: Monotonic per id: a consumer refuses a lower or equal version (drift refusal).

title.description: Human label. Deliberately not `name` (see the schema description).

level.description: The course's depth, as the catalogue shows it. A level is a label, not a gate.

locale.description: The language the shipped sources are written in (a variant axis: a render may override it).

kind.description: The artefact family. Pinned, like template.v1's `kind`: a future family (a workshop, a cohort pack) is a new contract, not a new value here.

renderer.description: The SLIDES renderer. `html` is always available and produces a self-contained deck per lesson; `typst` produces PDF slides and REFUSES by name (`typst not installed`) on an instance whose image does not carry the package -- never a silent fallback to html, and never a partial deck. There is no Marp and no Node toolchain behind either: a source is Markdown and the renderer builds the markup itself.

sources.description: The Markdown files this course ships, as a map of source KEY (what a lesson names) to FILE NAME (relative to the course directory). A source is Markdown, never a program: the file name is pinned to `.md`, so `.py`, `.html`, `.json` and every other extension are refused by the contract, and no consumer is ever handed a file it might execute.

summary.description: One or two sentences, shown in the outline. Plain text.

reading.description: The source KEY (not the file name) of the lesson's Markdown reading. Every key named here must exist in `sources`; the schema cannot express cross-key references, so the consumer's importer and this repo's contract test both refuse a key that is not declared.

slides.description: The source KEY of the lesson's Markdown slides (`---` separates one slide from the next).

video.description: An optional video for the lesson. Video production is F6: today a lesson that names one is refused by name unless the referenced footage asset exists in the library, is verified, commercial and unexpired -- which is the honest state, never a silently dropped lesson.

quiz.description: The lesson's quiz, as DATA. There is no interactive player in this slice: the quiz is rendered with the course and its shape is enforced before release (`answer` must be one of `options`, and every question carries an explanation).

answer.description: The correct option, verbatim one of `options`. The schema cannot express membership, so the consumer's quiz-shape check refuses an answer no option carries, BY NAME.

explanation.description: Why the answer is right. Required: a quiz without an explanation teaches nothing, and the check refuses it by name.

variables.description: Typed values a render supplies (the only free-text surface a course has). A variable a source names but does not declare is refused by name; a value carrying personal data is refused by the consumer's `course_variables` check.

enum.description: The allowed values of an `enum` variable. Required when `type` is `enum` (the consumer refuses an enum with no values).

assets.description: The licensed assets the course names, by role. Every value is an `asset:<key>` reference into the consumer's `factory.asset` library -- a raw URL is never a course value.

images.description: Image roles the course places (a cover, a diagram). The role name is free-form, the value is not.

footage.description: Video roles a lesson's `video.asset` may name (F6 owns production; the reference is what this contract carries).

outputs.description: The formats the released course carries. `html` always ships (the pack and every deck), `pdf` is declared when the renderer produces it, so a consumer never promises a format it cannot render.

kits.description: The brand kit codes this course is approved to render under: the kit supplies the palette, the fonts and the mandatory disclaimers. A kit not listed here refuses the render by name.
